newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NCC sees Swedish construction staying weak.
newsitem.headline: NCC sees Swedish construction staying weak.

text.p: Sweden's second largest construction company NCC said on Monday it expected weak trends in the Swedish construction market to continue for the rest of the year.

NCC returned to black figures in the first half of 1997, with a profit after financial items of 82 million crowns ($10.3 million) for the first half of 1997 compared to a loss of 82 million a year ago.
"The currently unfavourable trend in the Swedish construction market will continue throughout 1997," the company said in a statement.
NCC forecast it would post a full-year result, excluding restructuring costs, of 450-500 million crowns.
It expected that its ongoing merger with Swedish construction company Siab would mean restructuring costs of about 450 million crowns, for which NCC would make a provision in 1997.
Annual merger synergies of 400 million crowns would have a marginal impact on 1997 earnings, it said.

"The merger of Siab and NCC is proceeding well," Jan Sjoqvist, president and chief executive, said in the statement. "Despite intense merger activitiy, we have concluded that we have successfully upheld our market positions."
The swing to profit followed stronger sales and 301 million crowns in capital gains from selling companies and properties.
"A slight deterioriation in income from construction operations was more than offset by the sale of NK Cityfastigheter and Strabruken," it said.
Total construction orders rose six percent on a pro forma basis to 14.8 billion crowns in the first half, while its Swedish construction orders fell by 13 percent to 9.1 billion crowns.

Net sales rose to 11.94 billion crowns from 9.57 billion while operating income advanced to 298 million crowns from 114 million crowns and the result per share after full tax swung to a profit of 0.60 crown from a loss of one crown. -- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006
